1	# Agent definition
2	
3	## Why
4	
5	Blind planning exists because a planner that can read the code inherits the code's mistakes as constraints. Every workaround becomes an implicit requirement, and the feature gets shaped to fit the defect. Deriving the spec from intent alone makes disagreement between intent and implementation visible rather than silently absorbed. Phase 2 is not "soften the spec until it fits"; it is "name each disagreement and rule on it", with the code as the presumed-wrong party.
6	
7	## Engines
8	
9	A session runs on one engine, chosen per session or per phase:
10	
11	- Claude through the Agent SDK (Claude Code as a library, JavaScript build, inherited Claude Code login).
12	- GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi K3 through Berget AI (OpenAI-compatible) with our own loop and tools.
13	
14	The extension only sees `CodeSession`: send a prompt, stream events, answer permission requests, interrupt. Engines differ below that line.
15	
16	## Shape
17	
18	Three phases, each a separate session with its own system prompt and tool set. Handoff is files on disk, never conversation context.
19	
20	```
21	docs/intent/**  +  work item  →  spec.md  →  plan.md  →  code
22	                    (blind)      (reconcile)   (implement)
23	```
24	
25	## Phase 1: Blind plan
26	
27	Sees: feature description, domain brief (ubiquitous language, stack, constraints), `docs/intent/**`, one work item closure when ADO is connected.
28	Never sees: source, descriptive docs, PRs, build output.
29	
30	Until ADO is connected the feature description is typed by the user or picked from `docs/intent/**`. The agent plans the user story itself; the spec's task list is the source for the ADO tasks created under the story once ADO is connected (write-back, not read-only).
31	
32	Tools: Read/Glob scoped to `docs/intent/**`, `get_work_item(id)`, AskUserQuestion, optionally WebSearch. Bash denied by bare name (allow-lists only auto-approve; a bare-name deny removes the tool from context).
33	
34	Output `plan/<feature>.spec.md`: behaviour, invariants, edge cases, acceptance criteria with stable item IDs. No file paths. If `docs/intent/**` has nothing on the feature, output questions and stop.
35	
36	### get_work_item
37	
38	Hand-coded, read-only, Azure DevOps. Server-side filtering is the enforcement.
39	
40	- Include: title, description, parent chain, Goal/Actor/Impact/Behaviour/Example.
41	- Exclude: state, comments, tasks, linked PRs/commits/branches/builds, `System.*` and `Microsoft.VSTS.*` fields.
42	- Walks parents, children, related. Depth and total caps, cycle detection, deterministic ordering. Returns markdown. Snapshot to `plan/<feature>.context.md`.
43	- State is excluded deliberately: a Done item over drifted code is evidence for phase 2, not input to phase 1.
44	- Prose may leak file paths; accepted, or stripped in the tool.
45	
46	### Docs split
47	
48	`docs/intent/**` is phase 1 scope. Everything else is phase 2 only. Descriptive docs drift with the code in the same direction and arrive labelled as authority.
49	
50	## Phase 2: Reconcile
51	
52	Tools: Read, Glob, Grep. Edit/Write/Bash denied by bare name.
53	Input: spec + context + repo. Not the phase 1 transcript.
54	
55	Output `plan/<feature>.plan.md`, front-matter `status: draft|approved`, one verdict per spec item:
56	
57	| verdict | meaning |
58	|---|---|
59	| matches | nothing to do |
60	| drifted | correct the code |
61	| naive | amend spec, reason required |
62	| conflict | sources disagree, human decides |
63	
64	Authority order is fixed in the prompt: work item, then intent doc, then code. Amendments (`naive`) and drift findings are written back to `docs/intent/**` or the work item as an explicit output, so intent does not rot.
65	
66	## Retrieval
67	
68	A sub-session the planner calls with `retrieve(question, known, budget)` to keep file dumps out of its own context. Phase 2 first; phase 1 only when the intent tree or work-item graph outgrows the planner.
69	
70	- Locates and quotes, never interprets. Output is verbatim excerpts with provenance; the planner rules on them. A summary drops nuance silently, and the planner never sees what was left out.
71	- Tools are derived, not configured: the calling phase's tool set minus AskUserQuestion and anything that writes. Phase 1 retrieval is blind by construction.
72	- No user interaction, no recursion. "Needs X to answer" goes in `not_found`; the planner decides whether to ask. Depth 1.
73	- Result: `findings[]` (excerpt, source as `path#heading`, work item id or URL, one line on why it matches), `not_found[]` (what was looked for, where), `status: complete | partial | budget_exhausted`. Partial is a result, not an error.
74	- Written to `.agent/runs/<id>/retrieval/<n>.md`; the tool returns path, status and counts. Files on disk, not conversation context.
75	- Budget per call (tool calls, tokens), set by the planner. Exhaustion returns findings so far.
76	- Runs as a `CodeSession` under its own profile; a cheap model is fine because the task is search.
77	- Independent questions fan out as independent sessions, no shared state.
78	
79	## Phase 3: Implement
80	
81	Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, task state. Input is the approved plan file only, fresh session; refuses to start on `status: draft`. Drift items are work items alongside feature items.
82	
83	- Verification hook after edits: build scoped to the project owning the edited file, test selection, run on plan-item boundary; failure budget of N consecutive failed fixes per item, then stop and write the failure into the plan.
84	- Read-before-edit staleness: refuse to edit an unread file, re-read when changed underneath.
85	- Explicit task state so item 4 of 7 does not vanish.
86	- Done when the acceptance-criteria tests pass, not when the model stops.
87	
88	## Instructions
89	
90	Small shared core plus a per-phase file. Per-type rules inject via PreToolUse hook matched on the path at edit time.
91	
92	- Checkable rules (no `#region`, no AutoMapper/MediatR, nullable on, no `Any`) go to analyzers, `.editorconfig`, BannedApiAnalyzers, grep in the verification hook.
93	- Judgment rules (rule of three, earned abstraction) go to the prompt.
94	- A phase file over a page means the excess is checkable or is spec. Remove alternatives instead of instructing tool preference.
95	
96	## Coordination
97	
98	Claim registry `.agent/sessions/<id>.json`: claimed files, `plan_item_id`, `deadline` set by the session, heartbeat. PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write claims on first touch, denies if another live session holds the file and names who.
99	
100	- Session reports completion and releases the claim. Silence past `deadline` is the stale signal.
101	- Stale claims are flagged in the UI, never auto-released.
102	- Force-release posts a revocation message into the session. The session stops immediately, does not finish the in-flight edit, reports touched files.
103	
104	Checkpoints, opt-in: `checkpoint(reason)` scoped to files under the session's claims; `revert` hash-compares and refuses files that moved underneath. No git. Repeated checkpoints on one plan item mean the item was underspecified; log the reasons.
105	
106	Channels, non-blocking: `send(session, text)` returns immediately; notification is a one-line tail on the receiver's next tool result; `read_messages()` pulls the payload. Registry before channels. Cap thread length and escalate to the user.
107	
108	## Observability
109	
110	Run id, per-phase transcript, tool calls, token spend, checkpoint reasons under `.agent/runs/<id>/`.
111	
112	## Per-phase model
113	
114	Phase 1 wants the strongest reasoner, phase 3 wants throughput. Profiles carry engine, model and effort.
115	
116	## Parked
117	
118	- ADO: `get_work_item` and creating tasks under the user story from the spec's task list. No work items exist yet.
119	- Repo map for phases 2 and 3 (project list, public type index, folder conventions).
120	- Anthropic Messages API adapter under API key in the own-loop engine.
121	- Compaction in the own-loop engine.
122	- Retrieval in phase 1 (large intent tree, work-item graph, WebSearch).
123

2	
3	One file per feature, in rough build order. Each says what the feature does; `docs/intent/agent.md` says why. A feature is a candidate input for a Plan session.
4	
5	1. [reconcile-phase.md](reconcile-phase.md)
6	2. [implement-phase.md](implement-phase.md)

15	11. [own-loop-compaction.md](own-loop-compaction.md)

1	# Composer input
2	
3	The prompt box knows the workspace: files, selections and commands.
4	
5	- `@` in the composer opens a file picker over the workspace; a chosen file is inserted as a reference and sent as part of the prompt (path plus, for the Claude engine, the same `@file` syntax Claude Code understands; for the own loop, the file content is attached below the prompt with its path).
6	- "Add selection" button (and a command / context-menu entry in the editor) inserts the current editor selection with its file and line range.
7	- `/` lists the workspace's skills and commands from `.claude/`; picking one sends it as Claude Code would. On the own-loop engine a skill's `SKILL.md` is attached as context instead.
8	- Pasted or dropped images are sent as image content on engines that accept it, shown as thumbnails in the transcript.
9	- Draft text is kept per session, so switching tabs does not lose a half-written prompt.
10	- Up arrow in an empty composer recalls the previous prompt.
11	
12	Not included: mentions of other sessions, templates.
13

1	# AskUserQuestion
2	
3	The model asks structured questions and gets the answers back as tool input, on both engines.
4	
5	- Claude engine: the SDK routes the `AskUserQuestion` tool through the permission callback; the answer goes back as `updatedInput` with the answers filled in.
6	- Own-loop engine: a tool of the same name and schema (questions with header, options, multi-select).
7	- The transcript shows a question card per request: one group per question, single or multi select, free-text "Other". Submit resolves the request; the session status is `needs_human` until then.
8	- Answers are recorded in the run log like any tool result, so a replayed transcript shows what was asked and answered.
9	- Plan mode prompt drops the "ask in text and stop" rule once this exists.
10	
11	Not included: questions with previews, questions from subagents shown separately.
12

1	# Reconcile phase
2	
3	A session mode that compares an approved spec with the code and rules on every disagreement.
4	
5	- Starts from a plan session's spec; refuses a spec whose `status` is not `approved`.
6	- Tools: Read, Glob, Grep over the whole workspace; writes only `plan/<feature>.plan.md`.
7	- Input is the spec and the repo. It never sees the plan session's transcript.
8	- Output `plan/<feature>.plan.md` with front-matter `feature`, `spec`, `status: draft`, and one verdict per spec item, keyed by the spec's stable ids: `matches`, `drifted` (code is wrong, correct it), `naive` (spec is wrong, reason required), `conflict` (sources disagree, human decides).
9	- Authority order fixed in the prompt: work item, then intent docs, then code. Code is the presumed-wrong party.
10	- Every `drifted` verdict becomes a work item in the plan alongside the feature's tasks, with the files it concerns.
11	- `naive` verdicts are listed under an Amendments section as concrete spec changes, for the human to apply or reject; the phase never edits the spec.
12	- The plan bar shows the plan's status with Open and Approve; approval sets `status: approved`.
13	- Session status while working is `planning`; a finished turn is `needs_human`.
14	- Verdict counts per kind are shown in the transcript summary line.
15	
16	Not included: applying amendments automatically, ADO write-back, retrieval sub-sessions.
17

1	# Edit diff view
2	
3	Edits made by a session are reviewable as diffs, in the transcript and in the editor.
4	
5	- A permission card for Edit or Write shows the change as a unified diff instead of raw JSON: old and new text for Edit, full content for a new file, a diff against the current file for an overwrite.
6	- A completed Edit or Write tool row shows the same diff, collapsed, with the file path clickable to open the file at the first changed line.
7	- "Open diff" on a row opens VS Code's diff editor between the pre-edit content and the file as it is now.
8	- Pre-edit content is captured by the extension at permission time, not by the engine, so it works on both engines.
9	- A session's touched files are listed in the plan bar area (chat mode: a "Changed files" row) with per-file diff links.
10	
11	Not included: reverting from the diff, multi-file review flows, checkpoints.
12

1	# KiwiAgent
2	
3	VS Code extension that runs coding sessions with a choice of engine per session.
4	
5	- **Claude**: the Agent SDK's JavaScript build of Claude Code (`dist/cli.mjs`), spawned under Node with the login Claude Code already has. No native binary.
6	- **GLM-5.3-Flash / Kimi K3** through Berget AI (OpenAI-compatible): own loop with Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep and Bash. Read-only tools run without asking; the rest prompt, with "always allow" per tool and session. Needs an API key: run *KiwiAgent: Set API Key for Profile*.
7	
8	The three-phase design (blind plan, reconcile, implement) is the goal; `docs/intent/agent.md` is the definition.
9	
10	The sidebar has a Sessions view (every session, with status) and the Chat view: tabs for the sessions in play with a status icon (📐 planning, 🔧 implementing, 🧪 verifying, ✋ needs you, ⚠ error, ○ waiting), a `+` tab that opens the new-session screen, then the transcript. The model comes from settings (`kiwiAgent.activeProfile`, `kiwiAgent.planProfile`), not from the UI.
11	
12	Session modes:
13	
14	- **Chat**: work in the code with the full tool set.
15	- **Plan**: blind planning of one feature. The session can read `docs/intent/**` only, enforced at the tool call, and writes `plan/<feature>.spec.md` (behaviour, invariants, edge cases, acceptance criteria, tasks, open questions, stable item ids, `status: draft`). The first prompt is the feature or user story description. Writing the spec needs no permission prompt. A bar above the transcript switches between the spec (Plan) and the conversation (Chat), shows the spec's status and has Approve; the view follows the work: Chat while the planner responds, Plan when its turn ends. Approval sets `status: approved` in the front-matter, which later phases require.
16	
17	## Develop
18	
19	```
20	npm install
21	npm test          # no network or engine needed
22	npm run build     # dist/: extension, webview, cli.mjs, ripgrep
23	```
24	
25	F5 launches the Extension Development Host. Open the "KiwiAgent" view in the activity bar.
26	
27	## Develop with it
28	
29	Load the extension from this repo in your normal VS Code instead of a packaged copy:
30	
31	```
32	npm run link-dev   # installs the .vsix so VS Code registers it, then points the installed folder at this repo
33	```
34	
35	Reload the window once. From then on, after `npm run build` (or the `npm: watch` task) the extension notices its own bundle changed and offers "Reload Window". Sessions and the open session survive the reload; engines resume on the next prompt. `npm run unlink-dev` removes the link.
36	
37	Verify-on-stop for this repo (`.vscode/settings.json`) runs typecheck, tests and build after any `.ts` edit.
38	
39	## Install elsewhere
40	
41	```
42	npm run package   # kiwi-agent-<version>.vsix
43	code --install-extension kiwi-agent-<version>.vsix
44	```
45	
46	Requires Node in the environment only if `kiwiAgent.nodePath` is set; otherwise VS Code's own executable runs the engine in Node mode.
47	
48	## Settings
49	
50	- `kiwiAgent.profiles`: engine, model, effort per profile.
51	- `kiwiAgent.activeProfile`: profile name used for new sessions; `kiwiAgent.planProfile` overrides it for plan sessions.
52	- `kiwiAgent.nodePath`: Node executable for the Claude engine; empty uses VS Code's executable.
53	- `kiwiAgent.traceEngine`: one line per Claude engine message in the KiwiAgent output channel, to see what the engine sends (thinking deltas, status) when the UI shows nothing.
54	- `kiwiAgent.verify`: commands run when the model wants to stop after editing matching files, in the directory of the nearest `project` file. Failures go back to the model and it keeps working, up to `kiwiAgent.verifyFailureBudget` consecutive failures. Default: `dotnet build` of the `.csproj` owning any edited `.cs` file. Applies to every engine.
55	- Command *KiwiAgent: Set API Key for Profile* stores keys for profiles that declare `apiKeySecret`.
56	
57	Session events are logged to `.agent/runs/<session id>/events.jsonl` in the workspace; add `.agent/` to the workspace's `.gitignore`.
58

1	# Implement phase
2	
3	A session mode that carries out an approved plan, item by item, and stops when the acceptance criteria are proven.
4	
5	- Starts from an approved `plan/<feature>.plan.md`; refuses a draft. Fresh session, the plan file is its only input.
6	- Full tool set (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash) plus a task-state tool.
7	- Task-state tool: `list`, `start(id)`, `done(id, note)`, `blocked(id, reason)`. State lives in the plan file's front-matter so it survives reloads and is visible in git. Item N of M is always known.
8	- Works one plan item at a time in the plan's order; drift items and feature tasks are the same kind of item.
9	- Verification is on and cannot be switched off in this mode; it runs at each item boundary, scoped to the projects touched by that item.
10	- Failure budget per item: after N consecutive failed verifications the item is marked `blocked` with the last error, and the session moves on or stops if nothing else can proceed.
11	- Termination: the session is done when every acceptance criterion in the spec is bound to a passing test named in the plan, and no item is open. Stopping earlier is blocked the same way a failed verification is.
12	- The plan bar shows items done / blocked / open.
13	- Session status: `implementing` while working, `verifying` during verification, `needs_human` when an item is blocked or a permission is pending.
14	- Per-file-type rules (`kiwiAgent.rules`: match glob, text) are injected as context on the first Edit or Write of a matching file in a session, not in the system prompt.
15	
16	Not included: claims across sessions, checkpoints, ADO task updates.
17

---
feature: Commenitng a plan
status: draft
---

# Commenitng a plan

## Goal
A user reading the plan document a session just presented — the spec of a plan session, and the plan of a reconcile session — needs to push back on it without re-typing the whole document's faults into the composer. This feature lets the user attach a comment to any item of the presented document and strike the items they reject, gather those into one review, and send it back to the session as the next turn. The session revises the document: struck items are marked removed under their own ids, commented items are corrected. Approval stays the human's act, and a document the user has just objected to cannot be approved as if it were agreed.

## Behaviour
- B1: Every item of the presented plan document that carries a stable id (behaviour, invariant, edge case, acceptance criterion, task, open question, and in a reconcile plan each verdict) is individually addressable in the plan view: it can be commented on and it can be struck.
- B2: A comment is free text attached to one item. A document-level comment, attached to no item, is also possible, for "the goal is wrong" or "something is missing".
- B3: Striking an item marks it as rejected by the user. The item stays visible, shown as struck; nothing is deleted from the document by the act of striking.
- B4: A strike can be taken back while the review has not been sent.
- B5: Comments and strikes accumulate as a review that belongs to the user, not to the session: nothing reaches the model until the user sends it.
- B6: Sending the review ends the round: the session receives one turn containing, per item id, the comment text and whether the item was struck, plus any document-level comments and an optional free-text message written alongside them.
- B7: Send is offered while the session is waiting for the user. While a turn is running the review can still be composed, but not sent.
- B8: The session honours a strike by marking that item removed in the document, keeping its id and its place; it never renumbers the surviving items and never reuses the id of a removed item.
- B9: A struck item is not kept alive without the user hearing why: the session either marks it removed or asks the user about it.
- B10: A comment on an item is addressed by changing that item, not by adding a second item that says the same thing differently; the session may add new items with new ids for genuinely new behaviour the comment asks for.
- B11: The review survives switching tabs and reloading the window, per session and per document, the same way a half-written prompt does.
- B12: A sent review appears in the transcript as the user's turn, naming the ids commented on and the ids struck, so a replayed transcript shows what was objected to.
- B13: Approve is refused while the document has an unsent comment or strike; the user either sends the review or discards it first.
- B14: After a revision arrives, each strike sent in the previous round is shown as honoured when that item now reads as removed, and as unhonoured when the item is still live, so a strike the session ignored is visible rather than lost.
- B15: The plan bar shows the review state of the presented document: how many comments and how many strikes are waiting to be sent, and whether any strike from the last round is unhonoured.
- B16: Items marked removed are not work: later phases and item counts (items done / blocked / open) ignore them.
- B17: Reviewing behaves identically on both engines; it is an ordinary turn of the conversation, not an engine capability.

## Invariants
- I1: Commenting, striking or revising never renumbers an item and never reuses an id; ids only get added or marked removed.
- I2: A struck item is never silently deleted; it stays in the document, marked removed, with its id.
- I3: The plan document is the only record of the plan's content. Comments and strikes are review state; they never change the document's text by themselves — only the session's revision does.
- I4: No comment and no strike reaches the session other than through an explicit send by the user.
- I5: Sending a review against an approved document returns that document to draft; what later phases consume is only ever a document the user approved after the last revision.
- I6: Every sent review is recorded in the run log with the ids it touched, like any other turn.

## Edge cases
- E1: A comment is anchored to an id that the revised document no longer contains → the comment is not dropped; it is shown as unanchored and carried as a document-level comment, naming the id it was written against.
- E2: Send is pressed with no comment, no strike and no message → nothing is sent; the session is not disturbed.
- E3: An item is struck while other items reference it (a task covering it, an acceptance criterion resting on it) → the user is told which items reference it before sending, and the review still goes through; the revision is expected to resolve the dangling references.
- E4: Every item is struck → allowed; the session is asked to plan again from the feature description. No document is deleted on the user's behalf.
- E5: The document changes on disk while a review is being composed → comments and strikes re-anchor by id; any id that has disappeared follows E1.
- E6: The session is busy when the user finishes writing → Send stays unavailable, the review is kept, and it becomes sendable when the turn ends.
- E7: The session has ended or errored → the review is kept and the user is told it cannot be sent until the session accepts a prompt again.
- E8: A comment on an open question → it is simply the answer to that question; no separate answering mechanism.
- E9: An item that a previous round marked removed is un-struck → the review asks for it to be reinstated under its original id, not under a new one.
- E10: Two comments on the same item in one round → both are sent for that item, in the order written; neither replaces the other.
- E11: The document presented has no items yet (questions only, because intent was too thin) → the open questions are commentable and the goal is commentable; striking questions is allowed.

## Acceptance criteria
- A1: Given a presented plan document, when the user picks an item, then they can write a comment against it and the comment is shown attached to that item.
- A2: Given an item with a comment or a strike, when the user has not yet sent the review, then the session has received nothing and the document on disk is unchanged.
- A3: Given a struck item, when the review is sent and the session revises, then the document shows that item as removed with its original id, and no other item's id has changed.
- A4: Given a revision in which a struck item is still live, when the revision is presented, then that strike is shown as unhonoured.
- A5: Given comments on three items and a strike on one, when the review is sent, then the transcript shows one user turn naming those four ids and their texts.
- A6: Given an unsent comment or strike, when the user presses Approve, then approval is refused and the user is told to send or discard the review.
- A7: Given an approved document, when a review is sent against it, then its status is draft again.
- A8: Given a composed review, when the window is reloaded and the session reopened, then the same comments and strikes are still there.
- A9: Given a running turn, when the user has a composed review, then Send is unavailable and becomes available when the turn ends.
- A10: Given a comment written against an item that the revision removed entirely, when the revision is presented, then the comment is still visible as a document-level comment naming that id.
- A11: Given a document with items marked removed, when a later phase consumes it, then those items produce no work and are not counted as open.
- A12: Given the user strikes an item that a task references, when they send, then they were shown the referencing item beforehand.
- A13: Given the same review on either engine, when it is sent, then the session receives the same turn content.

## Tasks
- T1: Render the presented plan document as addressable items keyed by their stable ids, so a comment or a strike can be attached to exactly one item (B1, A1).
- T2: Hold a review — per session, per document — of item comments, document-level comments and strikes, kept across tab switches and reloads (B2, B5, B11, A2, A8).
- T3: Strike and un-strike, with the struck state shown on the item and the referencing-items warning before a send (B3, B4, E3, E9, A12).
- T4: Compose and send the review as one turn: ids, comments, strikes and the optional free-text message; nothing sent when the review is empty; Send gated on the session waiting for the user (B6, B7, E2, E6, E7, A5, A9, A13).
- T5: Instruct the session on how to answer a review: honour strikes by marking the item removed, keep ids stable, never renumber, never reuse, ask rather than silently keep a struck item, change the commented item rather than add a duplicate (B8, B9, B10, I1, I2, A3).
- T6: After a revision, reconcile the previous round against the new document: strikes honoured or unhonoured, comments re-anchored by id, unanchored comments kept as document-level (B14, E1, E5, A4, A10).
- T7: Guard approval on an outstanding review, and return an approved document to draft when a review is sent against it (B13, I5, A6, A7).
- T8: Show review state in the plan bar — pending comments, pending strikes, unhonoured strikes — and record each sent review in the run log (B15, I6).
- T9: Make items marked removed inert for consumers: excluded from item counts and from the work later phases pick up (B16, A11).

## Open questions
- Q1: Does this cover only the plan session's spec, or also the reconcile session's plan, including its verdicts? The spec above assumes both; if verdicts are commentable, does striking a verdict mean "this finding is wrong" or "do not do this work"?
- Q2: Should comments live in the plan document itself, so they survive outside the session and show up in version control, or stay purely session-side review state? The spec above assumes session-side.
- Q3: When the session disagrees with a strike, should it use the structured question mechanism, or is flagging the strike as unhonoured enough?
- Q4: Are comments one-shot (send, then re-comment if unsatisfied), or should they be threads the session replies to per comment and that stay open until resolved? The spec above assumes one-shot.
- Q5: Is the goal paragraph itself commentable and strikeable, or only the id-carrying items? The spec above makes it commentable but not strikeable.
- Q6: Should a review composed during a running turn queue and send itself when the turn ends, rather than waiting for the user to press Send?
- Q7: Can a removed item be resurrected by a later session on its own initiative, or only by an explicit user request (E9)?
- Q8: Does a review count as an ordinary turn for cost and context purposes, or should it be summarised to keep long review rounds out of the session's context?

The spec is written to `plan/commenitng-a-plan.spec.md`.

It treats "commenting a plan" as a **review round**: the user attaches free-text comments to any id-carrying item of the presented plan document, strikes the items they reject, and sends the whole lot back as one turn. Seventeen behaviours cover addressability, the draft-until-sent rule, sending, how the session must answer (mark struck items removed under their own id, never renumber, never silently keep a struck item), and the plan-bar/transcript visibility. Invariants protect id stability, the document as sole record of content, and the rule that approval only ever applies to the document as it stands after the last revision — sending a review against an approved document returns it to draft.

Edge cases handle comments orphaned by a revision, striking everything, striking a referenced item, and a busy or dead session. Nine tasks split it into rendering, review state, strike handling, sending, session instruction, post-revision reconciliation, the approval guard, visibility/logging, and making removed items inert for later phases.

Eight open questions remain — chiefly whether this also covers the reconcile plan's verdicts, whether comments should live in the document (and thus in version control) instead of session-side, and whether comments are one-shot or resolvable threads. The spec states the assumption it made for each, so you can overrule them cheaply.
